__FORCETOC__
'''Edwin Albert Power''' (12 February 1928 – 31 January 2004) was an [[:Category:English physicists|English physicist]] and an emeritus professor of [[applied mathematics]] at [[University College London]].<ref name=PhysicsToday>
{{cite journal
 |author1=David Craig |authorlink=David P. Craig
 |author2=Thuraiappah Thirunamachandran
 |year=2004
 |title=Edwin Albert Power
 |journal=[[Physics Today]]
 |volume=57 |issue=10 |pages=94
 |bibcode=2004PhT....57j..94C
 |doi=10.1063/1.1825282
 |doi-access=free
}}</ref> He made several contributions to the field of [[non-relativistic quantum electrodynamics]].<ref name=PhysicsToday/>

==Life==

Power was born in [[Honiton]], [[England]] on 12 February 1928.<ref name=PhysicsToday/> He obtained his BSc and MSc in mathematics from [[University College London]] in 1948 and 1949 respectively.<ref name=PhysicsToday/> He obtained his PhD under the supervision of [[John Currie Gunn]] at the [[University of Glasgow]], for which he obtained the [[Kelvin Prize]] in 1951 (the prize recognizes the best physics thesis of the year).<ref name=PhysicsToday/> His doctoral work concerned [[meson]] production from [[proton]]–proton [[collision]]s.<ref name=PhysicsToday/>

After his PhD, he worked at University College, where became professor of applied mathematics in 1967, and fellow in 1991.<ref name=PhysicsToday/> In 1953, he became a [[Commonwealth Fund Fellow]].<ref name=PhysicsToday/> He then spent two years in the United States, one at [[Cornell University]], one at [[Princeton University]].<ref name=PhysicsToday/> While at Princeton, he and [[John Archibald Wheeler|John Wheeler]] worked on electromagnetism and gravity, resulting in the proposition of "thermal [[geon (physics)|geons]]" in a paper published in ''[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]'' in 1957.<ref name=PhysicsToday/><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=Edwin A. Power
 |author2=John A. Wheeler
 |year=1957
 |title=Thermal Geons
 |journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]
 |volume=29 |issue=3 |pages=480
 |bibcode=1957RvMP...29..480P
 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.29.480
}}</ref>

Power then researched [[non-relativistic quantum electrodynamics]], particularly the interactions between radiation fields and particles, and developed several techniques.<ref name=PhysicsToday/> In 1959, he and [[Sigurd Zienau]] published a paper on the [[Coulomb gauge]] and its relation to the shape of [[spectral line]]s, non-relativistic [[Lamb shift]], and other phenomena in the ''[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A]]''.<ref name=PhysicsToday/><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=Edwin A. Power
 |author2=Sigurd Zienau
 |year=1959
 |title=Coulomb Gauge in Non-Relativistic Quantum Electro-Dynamics and the Shape of Spectral Line
 |journal=[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A]]
 |volume=251 |issue= 999|pages=427
 |bibcode = 1959RSPTA.251..427P
 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1959.0008
}}</ref> Power also studied the relation between [[quantum electrodynamics]] and various [[optics|optical]] and [[molecular physics|molecular phenomena]].<ref name=PhysicsToday/> In 1964, he published a book, ''Introductory Quantum Electrodynamics'', based on a series of lectures he gave in Chile and the US.<ref name=PhysicsToday/>

Power retired as a professor in 1993, but remained active in research until his death following a short illness.<ref name=PhysicsToday/> He died on 31 January 2004, in [[London]], England.
